patches.reason: Memory-only credentials: the encode (write) path of the server persistence schema drops `password`, so no persistent backend (web localStorage, desktop storage, drafts) ever receives one. Decoding still tolerates stored passwords from legacy files; a missing password reaches the existing authentication-failure path. Keystore persistence is owned by mobile issue #4. The embedded marker string 'mobile(M-002): password stripped at encode (memory-only)' survives minification and anchors V-cred dist verification.

patches.reason: Build-time seam so the vendored app can import the first-party host registry (@opencode-mobile/mobile-hosts, issue #3). The alias value is expressed as fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../../packages/mobile-hosts/src/index.ts", import.meta.url)) - importer-relative like the existing fonts-cjk stub, so the four .. segments land on the repository root's packages/; a bare relative string would resolve against the importer and miss. Dependency direction stays one-way: the vendored packages themselves do not depend on the first-party package; only this alias resolves the specifier at build time.

patches.reason: Adds an optional non-secret credential REFERENCE (http.credentialRef, inside ServerHttpBase) so a stored direct server can point at a keystore entry without storing any credential. The M-002 encode path still strips password; the reference is a pointer (mobile-credential:<id>), safe for every persistent backend, and resolves per session into memory only. Keystore-backed resolution is mobile issue #4; decoding tolerates absence for already-stored servers.
patches.verification: V3 tree equivalence with the patch registered; targeted probe scripts/verify-credential-ref.ts (schema round-trip keeps the reference, still strips password) plus the upstream persistence.test.ts file as regression.
patches.rebase: New patch (issue #3); rebase target is the ServerHttpBase struct in packages/app/src/runtime/server/persistence.ts, directly below the M-002 MemoryOnlyPassword field. Review note (issue #3, round 2): clearing semantics are 'undefined keeps, empty string clears' in the first-party registry (packages/mobile-hosts/src/registry.ts); whether a changed host target/identity invalidates or re-confirms its credentialRef is an issue #4 boundary decision, deliberately out of scope here. Issue #4 ruling recorded: whether a changed host target/identity invalidates its credentialRef is resolved as KEEP + explicit removal (the user unchecks remember or deletes the entry in the credential manager); see docs/design/units/connection.md 失效矩阵.

patches.reason: The connect dialog constructs a fresh connection object on save; without this patch the M-005 credential reference would be dropped on the first edit of a server (both the same-url add path and the key-changing replace path). The original's reference is forwarded into the new connection; the form never edits it (it is a non-secret pointer, there is no reference input in the dialog). The 'nothing changed' early-exit comparison deliberately stays without the reference: it is never user-editable here, so it cannot be the only change, and adding it would keep the dialog open pointlessly.

patches.reason: Shell bootstrap (issue #3). (1) Removes the assembly of location.origin into a ServerConnection: in this Android WebView shell the asset origin http://127.0.0.1:18090 is a static asset server, not an OpenCode service, so that connection could only fail its health check. The ?auth_token URL passthrough is inapplicable for the same reason (no assembled server to authenticate) and is removed with its cleanup helper. (2) Bootstraps the first-party host registry via createMobileHosts (fail-closed host-key stub + Null credential resolver; real counterparts are issues #6/#4) and injects hosts.upstreamConnections() - a solid-store-derived reactive value - as the app's servers prop; direct servers are added through the app's own dialog into the upstream persisted list. Not implemented via the VITE_OPENCODE_SERVER_MODE=none build-time variable on purpose: that would hide the behavior behind build configuration and complicate rebasing; this patch keeps the change visible and rebaseable in one place. M-007 amendment (issue #4): the entry now also creates the device credential vault client (createVaultClient over createWebMessageChannelTransport) with the handshake listener registered before first render - shape-validated only (event.origin is never consulted: embedder-posted messages carry an empty origin by platform construction), port captured inside the transport closure, acked immediately, later handshakes ignored - and passes the vault plus a vault-backed resolver into createMobileHosts. Before the ack the vault is unavailable (explicit state, no plaintext fallback).

patches.reason: Mounts the first-party SSH host manager (lazy import) in the settings 'servers' tab, above the upstream single-server panel and also when the upstream list is empty, so the first SSH host can be created. The manager reads the runtime bootstrapped by M-007 through getMobileHosts(). Known gap, documented in docs/design/interaction.md: in the multiple-servers layout the upstream nav replaces the 'servers' tab with per-server entries, so the manager is not reachable there; the injected extension rows themselves render through the upstream home/settings inventory (device verification: G13/G15).

patches.reason: Optional 'remember credential' for the connect dialog's password method (issue #4). The checkbox participates only when rendered AND the shell vault is available; the decision itself (truth table v3, 12 rows) lives in the first-party package (packages/mobile-hosts src/vault/remember.ts) so it is unit-tested and probe-able, and this patch only translates it into vault put/remove calls and the constructed connection. Add flow resolves the ref-bearing prior by normalized URL from server.list regardless of the connect method (password AND link/redeem) - otherwise the M-006 original is undefined on add and re-adding a remembered server would orphan its reference. Rows 2/12 abort the save with an inline needs-password message (never cast an empty value); the early-exit is forced off when the checkbox state differs from the prior's remembered flag; a failed put/remove keeps the dialog open with an inline error. Vault unavailable renders the checkbox disabled plus an explicit-state note - no plaintext fallback anywhere.

patches.reason: Hydration credential resolution (issue #4). After the persisted server list hydrates, stored http entries that carry a credential reference but no password get the password resolved from the shell vault and injected into the in-memory solid store ONLY - the M-002 encode path runs on every persist write, so the value can never reach a persistent backend; it merely spares re-typing within the session. Vault-level unavailability and per-entry corrupt/unsupported resolve to nothing and the server's own authentication flow takes over (docs/design/units/connection.md failure matrix; no plaintext fallback).

patches.reason: Platform fetch injection with the validated-follow policy (issue #5, decision 0002 D1). createSecureFetch from the first-party package keeps redirect:"follow" (legitimate same-origin reverse proxies keep working) and validates the FINAL response before body delivery: a cross-host final URL is refused with the body cancelled, an https-to-http downgrade is refused, and a request URL carrying userinfo credentials is refused before anything is sent. Coverage: platform.fetch feeds createServerTransport (API/SSE/binary reads) and the health checks; the upload XHR is validated separately by M-012 with the same rules, and the pairing-flow residual fetch surface (OpenCode.make + checkServerHealth(globalThis.fetch) in pairing.ts) is registered out-of-scope in docs/design/units/connection.md. Auth-header semantics are untouched (the Basic header is built upstream exactly as before); cross-origin redirect sub-requests already lose the Authorization header by browser spec, so the wrapper is the shell's own fail-closed layer, not a leak fix. The embedded marker 'mobile(M-011): platform fetch validated-follow (origin + downgrade checked before body delivery)' survives minification and anchors V-conn dist verification.
patches.verification: V3 tree equivalence with the patch registered; bun unit tests for the wrapper (packages/mobile-hosts/test/secure-fetch.test.ts: cross-host refuse, downgrade refuse, credential-URL refuse, direct pass, same-origin redirect pass); V2 build smoke + dist marker mobile(M-011) + scripts/verify-direct-connection.ts (full mode); device behavior BLOCKED (G3/G4/G5/G11).
patches.rebase: New patch (issue #5); rebase target is the createWebPlatform platform object literal in packages/app/src/runtime/platform/web.ts (the fetch field sits directly after the platform literal).

patches.reason: Validated-follow for the upload face (issue #5, decision 0002 D1). The attachment upload is the one request that bypasses the platform fetch seam (M-011) - it goes through XMLHttpRequest for progress and streaming - so the same URL policy from the first-party package is enforced here: userinfo credential URLs are refused before anything is sent (D-URL), and on load the FINAL xhr.responseURL must still be same-origin with the request and must not have downgraded https-to-http, else the body is rejected (SecureFetchError) instead of being read as the server's upload receipt. Cross-origin redirect sub-requests already lose the Authorization header by browser spec (the floor); this patch is the shell's own fail-closed layer on top.

patches.reason: Probe-classified connect errors on the save path (issue #5, decision 0002 D4). The endpoint probe is dispatched BEFORE the authoritative health check (so its classification is usually already resolved when the verdict arrives) but only chooses the error WORDING after the check failed - the health check stays the sole authority for whether a save proceeds, and a probe verdict can never pass a save it refused. Error-message precedence: the upstream mixed-content structural signal, then the check's own unauthorized flag (authoritative 401), then the probe's transport classification (dialog.server.error.<code>), then the generic upstream message as the EXPLICIT degrade when the probe is unavailable, answered ok, or conflicts with the real fetch - a classification is never fabricated. A userinfo credential URL is refused up front with the precise credential-url message (D-URL). App-i18n keys only (en base merged with the locale table; missing key falls back to en, then to the key itself) - the first-party mobile-hosts direct.error.* keys are a separate set for first-party UI surfaces (F5).
